query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and is intended to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance in its solidified solid-solution state, but its dynamic behavior across different temperatures and strain rates lacks a theoretical explanation. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could account for this behavior, and what controlled comparison within that regime would distinguish it? Specify predictions relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and a falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy has a higher stacking-fault energy (SFE) than the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy; this raised SFE shifts plasticity from deformation twinning to dislocation cross-slip across a broad temperature (200–700 K) and strain-rate (10⁻³–10³ s⁻¹) regime, stabilizing work hardening and preserving a favorable strength–ductility balance under dynamic loading.
generation.material_initial_state: As-solidified, single-phase FCC equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloys
generation.intervention: Uniaxial compression tests to 30% true strain under controlled temperatures (200–700 K) and strain rates (10⁻³–10³ s⁻¹)
generation.conditions: Identical heat treatment and sample geometry; strain recorded to 0.3 true strain; tests at five temperatures and five strain rates within the specified windows
generation.structural_mediator: Stacking-fault energy–mediated competition between twinning and cross-slip
generation.mechanism: Elevated SFE in the Co-free alloy suppresses twin nucleation and promotes cross-slip–driven dynamic recovery, yielding stable work-hardening and flow without serrations
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the Co-containing baseline, the Co-free alloy will exhibit a ≥20% reduction in twin volume fraction (TEM), a ≥10% increase in work-hardening rate, reduced flow stress serrations, and equal or improved ultimate strength and ductility across the tested regime
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy tested under identical thermal–mechanical conditions
generation.boundary: Temperature 200–700 K; strain rate 10⁻³–10³ s⁻¹; true strain ≤0.3; single-phase FCC microstructure
generation.uncertainty: Exact magnitude of SFE increase and correlated decrease in twinning are estimated; variation may occur at extreme ends of T and strain-rate limits

falsification_experiment.design: Perform paired uniaxial compression tests at 300 K and 10² s⁻¹ on Co-free and baseline alloys; deform to 0.25 true strain; characterize post-mortem by TEM and stress–strain analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Co-free alloy does not show a lower twin fraction and higher work-hardening rate (and/or shows equal or more serrations) relative to the baseline under these conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
